messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - Streaming decode workers OOM on cluster stream-prod-3. 5xx spike (18%) for streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Paged: jess (oncall).

jess (oncall): acked. jumping in. what’s the immediate customer impact? any hit to embeddings/other endpoints? :eyes: 

maria (ops): Containers on node ip-10-2-45-19 are in CrashLoopBackOff, repeating CUDA OOM during decode step. Not seeing app-level exceptions, just OOM from driver.

maria (ops): logs:
```
[2026-03-15T03:14:02Z] infer.decode: ERROR CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2G (attempt 3)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/decode.py", line 412, in decode_step
    kv_cache.append(tensor)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1200000000 bytes
```

sam (sre): Confirmed. Node saw sustained unbounded generation from a small set of streams ~60s each. CPU-backed fallbacks weren't used because model pinned to gpu-quant-1.

luca (support): Customer "AcmeRetail" reported ~20% request drops and truncated streams starting 02:58 UTC. They have a prompt that doesn't set max_tokens; UI change last week allowed unhindered streaming. Request ids: r-0a3f... correlated. Sending details to account team.

kai (eng-runtime): likely root cause = runaway generation with no max_tokens + continuous batching kept KV caches large, pushing memory past headroom. Quick mitigations: 1) enforce max_tokens cap at gateway (server-side) 2) enable streaming token throttling (per-connection) 3) fallback route to cpu-inference for long-running streams 4) roll restart affected decode pods.

jess (oncall): implement 1 & 2 now. can we push a gateway policy that sets default max_tokens=512 if unset? Also throttle per-connection to 20 tokens/sec.

kai (eng-runtime): patch ready. config snippet:
```yaml
- match: route: /v1/streaming/generate
  actions:
    - set_default: {max_tokens: 512}
    - throttle: {tokens_per_sec: 20}
```

jess (oncall): applying via console, deploying gate rules. deploy-bot, kick the rollout.

deploy-bot: Rolling update started for service gateway-config. 3/3 replicas updating.

maria (ops): cordoning node ip-10-2-45-19 and draining. kubectl commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon ip-10-2-45-19
kubectl drain ip-10-2-45-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Pods will restart on healthy nodes.

sam (sre): After applying throttle + default max_tokens, 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 3% in ~90s. Streaming error logs decreased. :white_check_mark:

kai (eng-runtime): pushing a small runtime guard to reject requests with explicit max_tokens > 4096 or missing + very long token-history. Will ship hotfix to canary in 10m. Also enabling fallback route to cpu-quant-1 for streams that exceed 120s.

luca (support): Noted customer impact window 02:58-03:10 UTC. Preparing incident notice for AcmeRetail with mitigation steps and offer of credits if data lost.

jess (oncall): handoff notes to next oncall. Current state: mitigation applied (throttle + default cap), affected nodes drained, error rate largely stable but watching. Action items:
- eng-runtime (kai): permanent validation for max_tokens + telemetry for token-length distributions
- eng-sre (sam): add alert for token-length anomaly and sustained per-connection memory growth
- support (luca): customer outreach + status page entry
- ops (maria): post-drain healthcheck and ensure no further OOMs on restarted nodes

jess (oncall): handing off to night oncall @kai in 20m. leaving summary in #incidents. :memo:

incident-bot: Handoff logged. Incident severity set to sev2. Assigned owners: kai (eng-runtime), sam (eng-sre).

kai (eng-runtime): quick followup - will open a ticket & deploy runtime guard to main cluster. Also going to add unit test to prevent regression.

sam (sre): will draft postmortem template and raw timeline. tagging for follow-up meeting. :eyes:

luca (support): sending customer summary draft to jess and account team.

jess (oncall): thanks everyone. monitoring for 30m then will close if stable. :thumbsup:
